title: Reading continuous-time signal notation
description: interpret $x(t)$ as a signal whose amplitude varies over time.

title: Reading piecewise-defined signals
description: determine which expression describes the signal on each time interval.

title: Recognizing periodicity and fundamental period
description: identify when a signal repeats and determine its smallest repeating interval.

title: Forming the magnitude-squared signal
description: compute $|x(t)|^2$ as the quantity used in energy and power calculations.

title: Evaluating a definite integral
description: compute accumulated quantity over a finite interval.

title: Evaluating improper integrals
description: evaluate or interpret integrals taken over infinite intervals.

title: Understanding limit-based averaging
description: understand an average as a limit taken as the time window extends to infinity.

title: Integrating common signal expressions
description: handle constants, polynomials, and decaying exponentials when evaluating integrals.

title: Interpreting signal size as a scalar
description: understand signal size as a scalar that reflects both amplitude and duration.

title: Relating instantaneous power to amplitude
description: understand why pointwise power depends on the square of a signal's amplitude.

title: Connecting power and energy
description: interpret power as the rate of energy change and energy as accumulated power over time.

title: Computing total signal energy
description: compute total signal energy with $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|x(t)|^2\,dt$.

title: Recognizing signals with infinite energy
description: identify when a signal does not decay enough for total energy to converge.

title: Computing average signal power
description: compute long-run average power for signals whose total energy is infinite.

title: Computing periodic-signal power over one period
description: replace the long-time average with a one-period average when the signal is periodic.

title: Choosing between energy and power measures
description: decide whether total energy or average power is the meaningful descriptor for a given signal.

title: Classifying energy signals
description: identify signals whose total energy is finite and nonzero.

title: Classifying power signals
description: identify signals whose average power is finite and nonzero.

title: Splitting piecewise energy integrals
description: break an energy integral into interval-by-interval pieces and sum the contributions.

title: Computing energy of a finite-energy signal
description: apply the energy formula to a signal with finite support or exponential decay.

title: Computing power of a periodic signal
description: apply the one-period power formula to a repeating waveform such as a ramp or sawtooth.

title: Distinguishing decay from repetition
description: recognize that decaying signals tend to be energy signals, while repeating signals tend to be power signals.
